To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a semi-parametric transfer learning method based on Gaussian processes that can adaptively estimate the similarity between a target task and source tasks, and then select appropriate source tasks to improve target task’s performance, and our approach is evaluated on both synthetic and two real-world datasets
we propose a novel transfer learning algorithm based on GPs, which can adaptively transfer the knowledge between tasks.

(1) we propose a new transfer kernel based on Gaussian Processes, which is able to adapt to the target task; (2) the proposed kernel can be applied to both regression and classification problems, and can be used to transfer knowledge from one domain to another; (3) the proposed kernel is more robust than the existing kernels, as shown in the experiment results; (4) we propose a novel transfer learning framework that is able to automatically estimate the similarity between a target and a source task
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. How to learn from multiple related tasks? How to adaptively transfer the knowledge from a related task to a target task? How to ensure that a source task is useful for a target task?
the transferability of knowledge, i.e., how to ensure a “safe” transfer of knowledge in a transfer learning setting.
the following two questions: (1) How to adapt the transfer schemes by learning the task relationships in an automatic manner? (2) How to ensure a safe transfer of knowledge in transfer learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is capable of adaptively learning the transfer learning schemes, thus achieving better performance than the state-of-the-art transfer learning methods.

the proposed AT-GP method is an adaptive transfer learning algorithm, which can adaptively estimate the similarity of two tasks and then transfer the knowledge from a source to a target task in an adaptive way.
our proposed method can be used to learn the similarity between a pair of tasks, and then automatically adapt the transfer schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully formulated the transfer learning problem from a Bayesian perspective and have proposed a new transfer learning scheme, which can be used in a wide range of transfer learning problems.
we propose a novel semi-parametric transfer learning method, which can adaptively learn the transfer learning schemes and then ensure a safe transfer of knowledge.
we propose a novel semi-parametric kernel for transfer learning and propose a new learning strategy, which can be easily applied to many existing transfer learning algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfer learning problem can be formulated as a Bayesian model, and the similarity between tasks is crucial in transfer.
it can help to avoid negative transfer, and thus ensure a safe transfer of knowledge.
the proposed AT-GP algorithm is a general framework that can be used to learn transfer models in various scenarios.
